records.name: Claude Code (March source snapshot)
records.repo: keejkrej/claude-code (fork of public mirror of leaked src/) @ 3a854557e01e
records.license: Proprietary (exposed via npm source map; not licensed for reuse)
records.language: TypeScript on Bun (React 19 + forked Ink TUI)
records.one_liner: Anthropic's terminal coding agent: a ~515 kLOC single-binary product whose small async-generator loop (src/query.ts) is wrapped by a layered permission engine, cache-optimized context ladder, hooks/skills/plugins/MCP, subagents and a stream-json control protocol shared by SDK, IDE, bridge and cloud surfaces.

dims.loop: Async-generator queryLoop in src/query.ts rebuilds one State record per continue, tagged with typed Terminal(10)/Continue(8) transitions; tools start while the model streams; prompt-too-long/max-output errors are withheld until collapse-drain, reactive compact, token escalation or resume nudges fail; mid-turn steering via a global queue; fallback model after repeated 529s.
dims.providers: Anthropic Messages API only via @anthropic-ai/sdk, routed to first-party, Bedrock, Vertex or Foundry by CLAUDE_CODE_USE_* env; heavy use of Anthropic-only features (adaptive thinking signatures, cache_edits, 1h/global cache scope, task_budget, deferred tools, advisor); per-model USD from static tier tables.
dims.tools: ~40 built-ins as Zod Tool objects via buildTool fail-closed defaults; consecutive concurrency-safe calls batched (cap 10), Bash-only sibling abort; pipeline zod→validateInput→PreToolUse hooks→permission→call→spill >50k-char results to files with 2kB preview→PostToolUse; ToolSearch defers MCP tools beyond 10% of context.
dims.context: System prompt split at a dynamic cache boundary with memoized sections; CLAUDE.md hierarchy (managed/user/project/local, @include depth 5) prepended as a user message, git status appended; ladder: tool-result budget→microcompact (incl. cache_edits)→autocompact via cache-sharing forked summarizer with file/skill rehydration; MEMORY.md auto-memory with side-query relevance.
dims.state: Append-only JSONL per session under ~/.claude/projects/<cwd>/ with parentUuid chains, per-subagent sidechain files and spilled tool-results; continue/resume/fork/resume-at; interrupted-turn detection appends a continue message; file-history snapshots (max 100) back /rewind; user message persisted before each API call.
dims.safety: Modes default/acceptEdits/plan/bypassPermissions/dontAsk plus auto (LLM classifier) and bubble; rules from 8 sources incl. managed policy; ordered pipeline with bypass-immune .git/.claude paths; ~7 kLOC Bash static analysis; opt-in sandbox-runtime (Seatbelt/bubblewrap) for shell with domain allowlist; CanUseToolFn seam for dialog, SDK callback or MCP tool.
dims.extensibility: 27 hook events with command/prompt/http/agent hook types; SKILL.md skills (inline or forked) unified with slash commands in one Command type; plugin.json bundles commands/agents/skills/hooks/MCP/LSP/output styles distributed via marketplaces; MCP client with 7 transports, OAuth, elicitation, channels; `claude mcp serve`.
dims.multi_agent: Agent tool runs the same query() in-process with cloned context, no-prompt permissions, sidechain transcripts and optional git-worktree isolation; background agents report via task-notifications drained mid-turn; experimental agent teams with file mailboxes and tmux/iTerm/in-process teammates; coordinator, fork and workflow modes gated or absent.
dims.surfaces: Ink TUI; -p headless with text/json/stream-json; bidirectional stream-json + 21-subtype control_request protocol reused by Agent SDKs, IDE extensions, Remote Control bridge (child CLI with --sdk-url) and cloud sessions; MCP server; Chrome MCP; direct-connect HTTP server gated out; ACP only via Zed's external adapter.
dims.observability: Opt-in OpenTelemetry metrics/logs (OTLP, Prometheus) and beta traces with interaction/llm_request/tool spans; first-party and Datadog analytics with 900+ tengu_* names and GrowthBook gates; cost tracker restored on resume; loop checkpoints and startup profiler; VCR record/replay fixtures and ablation baseline for evals.

builds_on: Ink (forked into src/ink) + React 19 with React Compiler; pure-TS Yoga port
used_by: Claude Agent SDK Python/TS (spawns the CLI binary over stream-json)
Goose claude_code provider (spawns claude with stream-json directly, no SDK)
Cline ClaudeCodeProvider and Claude Code JSONL session import
Zed claude-agent-acp (third-party ACP adapter over the Agent SDK)
claw-code (Rust re-implementation guided by the leaked file inventory)
key_insights: The leak is a source-map reconstruction of the external build: 89 bun:bundle feature() flags dead-code-eliminate whole modules (reactive compact, context collapse, REPL/Workflow tools, `claude server`), so call sites are visible but implementations absent; .tsx files are React Compiler output with USER_TYPE constant-folded to "external".

Prompt-cache preservation shapes the architecture: CLAUDE.md and date go into a prepended user message rather than the system prompt; the system prompt is split at a dynamic boundary with memoized sections; built-in tools are sorted as a cache prefix ahead of MCP tools; and compaction/summary forks reuse the parent's exact CacheSafeParams.

The loop is a typed state machine: each continue rebuilds one State record tagged with a transition reason, and recoverable API errors are withheld from SDK streams until collapse drain, reactive compact, max-token escalation and up to three resume nudges have failed. Code comments document production retry spirals that this structure prevents.
Tools start executing while the model is still streaming (StreamingToolExecutor), with batching of consecutive concurrency-safe calls (cap 10); only Bash failures abort sibling tools.

One stream-json + control_request protocol (21 control subtypes, defined as Zod schemas inside the CLI) serves both SDKs, IDE extensions, Remote Control bridge children (--sdk-url) and cloud sessions; in-SDK MCP tools ride the same channel as mcp_message requests.

Permission is a single CanUseToolFn seam with three implementations (React dialog; SDK can_use_tool raced against PermissionRequest hooks; MCP permission-prompt tool) on top of an ordered rule pipeline with bypass-immune paths and an LLM auto-mode classifier. The OS sandbox is opt-in and covers shell commands only.
Large tool outputs are spilled to per-session files with a 2 kB preview instead of being truncated, and replacement records are persisted so that resume replays byte-identical context.

features_notes.in_process_sdk: Custom tool callbacks run in-process; the full harness runs in the CLI child.
features_notes.os_sandbox: Optional shell sandbox; historical CLI snapshot and current SDK configuration are distinct evidence scopes.

records.name: Claude Agent SDK (Python + TypeScript)
records.license: Python: MIT; TypeScript: Anthropic Commercial Terms of Service
records.language: Python (anyio); TypeScript (published npm bundle only, no source in repo)
records.version: Python 0.2.166 (bundles CLI 2.1.299); TS 0.3.299 (parity with CLI 2.1.299; npm latest 0.3.300)
records.one_liner: Thin Python/TS clients that spawn the Claude Code native binary and drive it over stream-json stdio with a bidirectional control protocol, exposing permission callbacks, hook callbacks and in-process MCP custom tools.

dims.loop: No loop of its own: query() and ClaudeSDKClient stream SDKMessages from the child CLI's QueryEngine loop. Turns are steered with user messages and control requests (interrupt, set_model, set_permission_mode, stop_task, rewind_files); each run ends with a typed result (success, error_max_turns, budget or structured-output errors).
dims.providers: Inherits Claude Code's Anthropic-only model layer (first-party, Bedrock, Vertex, Foundry via env). Options for model, fallback_model, thinking (adaptive/enabled/disabled), effort and betas are translated into CLI flags.
dims.tools: Built-in Claude Code tools are selected via tools/allowed_tools/disallowed_tools. Custom tools use @tool + create_sdk_mcp_server: a real mcp.server.Server in the host process, bridged to the CLI's mcp_message control requests by SdkMcpBridge. External MCP servers pass through --mcp-config.
dims.context: System prompt can be replaced, appended, preset or loaded from a file. Since TS 0.1.0, no default system prompt or filesystem settings are loaded unless setting_sources asks for them. Compaction, CLAUDE.md and memory remain the CLI's. get_context_usage reports token usage.
dims.state: The CLI writes JSONL locally; the SDK adds resume/continue/fork_session/resume_session_at and list/read/rename/tag/delete helpers over that JSONL. A SessionStore protocol (append/load required) mirrors transcripts to S3/Redis/Postgres after the local write. File checkpointing is enabled by env flag, with rewind_files.
dims.safety: The async can_use_tool callback receives tool, input, suggestions and blocked_path, and returns allow (with updated input or permissions) or deny (optionally interrupting). Also permission_mode and sandbox settings merged into --settings. PermissionRequest hooks race the callback inside the CLI. Flag values use the --flag=value form to block argv injection.
dims.extensibility: Hook callbacks are registered as opaque IDs in initialize (10 typed events in Python) and invoked via hook_callback. Also programmatic agents, skills selection, local plugin dirs, setting sources, and extra_args passthrough for new CLI flags.
dims.multi_agent: Inherits CLI subagents: AgentDefinition dicts are sent in initialize, task_started/progress/notification events are tracked, and stop_task control is available. Worktree isolation and agent teams come only through CLI features and flags.
dims.surfaces: Python and Node libraries spawning a bundled or PATH native binary over stdio. TS adds a browser SDK (WebSocket/SSE to remote CLIs), bridge/core subpaths and prewarm() process pools. Consumed by AI SDK, Mastra, MS Agent Framework, DeepSeek Harness, OpenClaw and Zed's ACP adapter.
dims.observability: Injects the active OpenTelemetry traceparent into the CLI environment so CLI spans join the host trace. Result messages carry usage, total_cost_usd, per-model usage, duration and permission_denials. Optional stderr callback; CLI OTel exporters are configured via env.

builds_on: Claude Code CLI native binary (Python wheel bundles CLI 2.1.299; TS uses per-platform optional-dependency binaries) driven over stdio stream-json
mcp Python SDK / @modelcontextprotocol/sdk (in-process SDK MCP servers)
key_insights: Not a library port: both SDKs spawn the CLI (bundled native binary first, PATH fallback) with --input-format/--output-format stream-json and speak the CLI's own control protocol. The TS GitHub repo contains no SDK source, only a changelog and SessionStore examples.
Custom tools run in the host process as real MCP servers, but the CLI child calls them through mcp_message control requests. The loop, prompts and permission engine stay in the child process.
Python exposes only 10 of the CLI's 27 hook events as typed callbacks. Hooks are registered as opaque callback IDs in the initialize request and dispatched through hook_callback.

Since TS 0.1.0, SDK sessions start without Claude Code's system prompt or filesystem settings unless a preset or setting_sources opts in. This is a deliberate isolation choice that differs from the CLI's defaults.
SessionStore extends durability beyond local disk: transcript entries are mirrored to external stores after the local write succeeds, and adapters are checked by a 13-contract conformance suite.
Versioning is in lockstep with the CLI (SDK 0.3.N matches CLI 2.1.N). The embeddable API is still 0.x and has removed APIs (unstable_v2_*), so it is less stable than the product it wraps.

features_notes.in_process_sdk: Custom tool callbacks run in-process; the full harness runs in the CLI child.
features_notes.os_sandbox: Optional shell sandbox; historical CLI snapshot and current SDK configuration are distinct evidence scopes.
features_notes.acp: Third-party adapters exist; ACP is not a native SDK protocol.

records.name: claw-code
records.one_liner: A community Rust re-implementation of a Claude-Code-shaped CLI agent, created the day of the leak and structurally guided by the leaked file inventory. It adds multi-provider support but has a simplified loop, compaction and permission model.

dims.loop: Synchronous ConversationRuntime::run_turn loop. ApiClient::stream returns a collected Vec of events per request; tool_use blocks run sequentially with Pre/Post hooks and permission checks. Supports a steer queue, interrupts and max_iterations; auto-compaction is checked every iteration.
dims.providers: ProviderKind covers Anthropic, xAI and OpenAI (OpenAI-compatible chat completions, including local models), with model alias tables and per-provider feature diagnostics. Prompt-cache events are tracked for Anthropic.
dims.tools: About 60 tool specs mirroring Claude Code names (bash, file tools, glob/grep, WebFetch, TodoWrite, Skill, Agent, Task*, Team*, Cron*, LSP, MCP) plus Worker* and Git* tools, dispatched by string match in an 11 kLOC tools crate.
dims.context: System prompt is assembled from CLAUDE.md, .claw/ files, CLAW.md and AGENTS.md. Compaction is heuristic: it keeps the last 4 messages and replaces older ones with a summary of counts and tool names, with no LLM call.
dims.state: Sessions persist as JSONL (snapshot plus append), including compaction records, with resume and session-control commands. No rewind or file checkpointing was found.
dims.safety: Codex-like PermissionMode values ReadOnly/WorkspaceWrite/DangerFullAccess/Prompt/Allow, a permission enforcer, a policy engine and a Bash validation module. The sandbox uses Linux-only unshare user namespaces, with an optional network namespace.
dims.extensibility: A plugins crate with plugin hooks and lifecycle, an MCP stdio client and tool bridge, SKILL.md skills, 3 hook events (PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure) and a slash-command crate.
dims.multi_agent: The Agent tool spawns an OS thread that runs a fresh ConversationRuntime with restricted tools and persists a terminal-state manifest. Team, cron and task registries plus worker boot/observe tools exist. No worktree isolation.
dims.surfaces: An interactive claw REPL and one-shot prompt with JSON output; an MCP server mode exposing its tools; ACP is status-only. The sdk crate speaks the separate gajae-code broker protocol, not Claude's.
dims.observability: Runtime emits turn and iteration events and tracks usage and cost. The telemetry crate only builds client identity and request profiles. A mock Anthropic service and a 12-scenario mock parity harness provide behavioural tests. No OpenTelemetry.

builds_on: Claude Code leaked source (file-inventory snapshots in src/reference_data and leak-named Python stubs guided the port)
used_by: Gajae-Code / LazyCodex agent harnesses (the README says they maintain the repo; the sdk crate implements the gajae-code broker wire protocol)
key_insights: Created on 2026-03-31, the day of the leak. Its Python reference_data inventories of the original archive (module counts per subsystem) give an independent baseline. That baseline exposes additions in leak mirrors: for example, services has 130 modules in the inventory versus 136 in the keejkrej fork, the difference being an x402 payment module.

Fidelity is shallow on the hard parts: tool execution is sequential, streaming is collected rather than incremental, and compaction is a non-LLM heuristic. Claude Code instead overlaps tool execution with streaming and summarizes with a cache-sharing forked agent.
It diverges from Claude Code on purpose: it supports Anthropic, xAI and OpenAI-compatible providers and natively loads AGENTS.md and CLAW.md alongside CLAUDE.md.
The permission vocabulary (ReadOnly/WorkspaceWrite/DangerFullAccess) and the Linux unshare sandbox resemble Codex more than Claude Code's rule-based modes and sandbox-runtime.

The README describes it as an agent-maintained 'museum exhibit'. Parity is tracked with a deterministic mock Anthropic service and 12 scripted scenarios. It has no stream-json control protocol, so it is not a drop-in target for Agent SDK consumers.
